terms.comment: Prohibitions take nōlī + infinitive, nē + perfect subjunctive, or in everyday speech nē + present subjunctive (Traupman 33, as cited).

phrases.english: Don’t touch, Theo; they’re very hot.
Leave it alone; it isn’t yours.

phrases.latin: aliēnō manum abstineat, sua servet dīligenter
phrases.english: let him keep his hands off what is another’s, and look carefully after his own

phrases.latin: Nōlī tangere; venēnātus est hic fungus.
phrases.english: Don’t touch it; this mushroom is poisonous.

sources: Lewis & Short: tango
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 33, 325.
